title: Pride and Prejudice
author: Jane Austen
authorBio: Jane Austen turned the manners and marriage markets of Regency England into comedy with a sharp moral eye. Her novels were published between 1811 and 1817.
synopsis: At Longbourn, Elizabeth Bennet dismisses the reserved Mr. Darcy after a disastrous first meeting. As her sisters' prospects shift and an old accusation resurfaces, Elizabeth must reconsider what pride has concealed from them both.

title: Frankenstein
author: Mary Shelley
authorBio: Mary Shelley wrote Frankenstein while still a teenager and later built a career as a novelist and editor. Her fiction often tests the cost of ambition against human responsibility.
synopsis: Scientist Victor Frankenstein assembles a living being in Ingolstadt, then abandons him in terror. Rejected by every family he approaches, the creature pursues his maker across Europe and demands an answer for his loneliness.

title: Dracula
author: Bram Stoker
authorBio: Bram Stoker managed a London theater while writing novels and short fiction. His best-known book gathers letters, diaries, and newspaper reports into a single mounting threat.
synopsis: Solicitor Jonathan Harker arrives at a Transylvanian castle whose host never seems to eat and casts no reflection. Once Count Dracula reaches England, Mina Murray and a small circle of friends trace a series of strange illnesses back to his voyage.

title: The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes
author: Arthur Conan Doyle
authorBio: Arthur Conan Doyle was a Scottish physician whose detective stories made close observation into a form of drama. He also wrote historical novels, adventure fiction, and public essays.
synopsis: From a vanished bridegroom to a royal photograph, twelve cases pull Dr. Watson back into Holmes's London rooms. Each puzzle hinges on an overlooked detail that places a client's reputation, livelihood, or life in danger.

title: Moby-Dick
author: Herman Melville
authorBio: Herman Melville drew on years at sea for novels that range from adventure to philosophical inquiry. Moby-Dick found its broad readership long after its original publication.
synopsis: Ishmael signs aboard the Pequod in Nantucket, expecting a whaling voyage under Captain Ahab. He soon learns the captain means to chase the white whale that took his leg, no matter what the hunt costs the crew.

title: The Time Machine
author: H. G. Wells
authorBio: H. G. Wells used speculative fiction to examine class, power, and scientific change. His early novels helped establish the modern language of science fiction.
synopsis: A London inventor reaches the year 802,701 and befriends Weena, a woman among the carefree Eloi. When the subterranean Morlocks steal his machine, he must descend beneath their ruined world to recover his only route home.

chapters.title: The Trap of the White Sphinx

title: Little Women
author: Louisa May Alcott
authorBio: Louisa May Alcott supported her family through writing and nursing before the March sisters made her famous. Her stories draw on the work and ambitions of women in her own household.
synopsis: With their father away at war, Meg, Jo, Beth, and Amy March find ways to grow up without losing one another. In Concord, small acts of generosity and painful mistakes test each sister's idea of the life she wants.

title: The Great Gatsby
author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
authorBio: F. Scott Fitzgerald chronicled wealth and aspiration in American fiction of the 1920s. His precise, restless prose gave the Jazz Age one of its enduring portraits.
synopsis: Nick Carraway rents a modest Long Island house beside Jay Gatsby's glittering estate. Gatsby's elaborate parties conceal a plan to reclaim Daisy Buchanan, and Nick watches that dream collide with money, marriage, and a fatal drive.

title: A Christmas Carol
author: Charles Dickens
authorBio: Charles Dickens published serial fiction that brought crowded Victorian streets and social inequality to a vast audience. He also campaigned for children's welfare and better public institutions.
synopsis: On Christmas Eve in London, the miser Ebenezer Scrooge is visited by his dead business partner, who warns that three spirits will follow. Their journeys through memory, present hardship, and a lonely future give him one night to change course.

title: Treasure Island
author: Robert Louis Stevenson
authorBio: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote adventure stories, essays, and travel books while living across Britain, Europe, and the Pacific. His fiction often lets a young narrator discover adult danger firsthand.
synopsis: Young Jim Hawkins finds a map in a dead sailor's chest at the Admiral Benbow Inn. A voyage to recover the buried treasure turns perilous when Jim overhears the ship's cook, Long John Silver, planning a mutiny.

title: Jane Eyre
author: Charlotte Brontë
authorBio: Charlotte Brontë published poetry and fiction under the name Currer Bell. Her novels joined intense inner life to questions of work, independence, and social rank.
synopsis: After a harsh childhood at Gateshead and Lowood, Jane Eyre becomes a governess at Thornfield Hall. Her growing bond with Edward Rochester is threatened by strange laughter and a hidden secret that could cost Jane her hard-won independence.

title: The Call of the Wild
author: Jack London
authorBio: Jack London drew on his travels and manual labor for stories of survival and social conflict. His Alaska fiction remains closely tied to the Klondike Gold Rush.
synopsis: Stolen from a comfortable California home, Buck is sold into sled work in the Yukon. As brutal handlers and rival dogs reshape his life, his attachment to prospector John Thornton pulls against an older instinct for the forest.

title: The Tide Clerk
author: Mara Ellison
authorBio: Mara Ellison grew up around working harbors and writes mysteries about the records people leave behind. The Tide Clerk is her first novel.
synopsis: When a ledger vanishes from Bellwether's harbor office, clerk Ada Voss finds its last entry names a ferry passenger who died twenty years earlier. Her search through tide tables exposes a smuggling route that still carries people at night.

title: The Glass Buoy
author: Mara Ellison
authorBio: For her second Bellwether mystery, Mara Ellison drew on accounts of salvage crews and disputed wrecks. She writes from a small coastal town.
synopsis: A diver brings Ada Voss a sealed buoy recovered outside Bellwether, with a fresh note inside from a captain presumed lost at sea. Ada follows the buoy's drift back to a private salvage crew whose next job could erase the harbor's only witness.

title: Orbit of Ashes
author: Keon Park
authorBio: Keon Park writes near-future fiction about ordinary workers inside extraordinary machines. He studied mechanical engineering before turning to novels.
synopsis: After an orbital refinery burns, mechanic Leda Saye survives in a maintenance pod with enough air for two days. Her distress call reaches a rescue ship, but its crew has orders to destroy the refinery's flight recorder before she can hand it over.

title: The Silent Apogee
author: Keon Park
authorBio: Keon Park returns to orbital infrastructure in his second Cinder Orbit novel. His stories follow technicians forced to question the missions they maintain.
synopsis: Leda Saye is hired to inspect a weather station that has gone dark above the Indian Ocean. Its last transmission includes a voice message from her dead brother, drawing her into a dispute over who controls the planet's storm forecasts.

title: Small Hours at Mercy Street
author: Nina Calder
authorBio: Nina Calder writes about family obligations and the places where people rebuild their routines. Her fiction has appeared in independent literary magazines.
synopsis: After her mother's stroke, June Mercer takes over the overnight shift at a laundromat in Pittsburgh. The regular customers know pieces of her mother's past that June never heard, and their stories force her to reconsider a long-avoided move.

title: Maps for the Missing
author: Avery Chen
authorBio: Avery Chen writes investigative thrillers with an eye for civic systems and overlooked neighborhoods. Chen lives in the Pacific Northwest.
synopsis: Cartographer Ellis Ward notices that three city evacuation maps omit the same apartment block in Tacoma. Days before a coastal drill, a tenant disappears there, and Ellis must find who altered the maps before the building is sealed.

title: When the Orchards Froze
author: Elise Varga
authorBio: Elise Varga researches rural labor and food history. Her narrative histories connect family archives with changes in land and industry.
synopsis: In 1917, an early freeze devastated apple growers around Brackenford. Varga follows Nora and Ellis Vale through farm ledgers and family diaries as they organize credit, storage, and a shared rail shipment to survive the winter.

title: An Atlas of Rain
author: Samira Dey
authorBio: Samira Dey writes personal essays about migration, memory, and the work of making a home. Her first book grew out of notebooks kept across three cities.
synopsis: From monsoon afternoons in Kolkata to wet bus stops in Seattle, Samira Dey charts the weather that marked her family's moves. A box of damaged photographs prompts her to revisit each address and ask what her parents chose to leave unsaid.

title: The Brass Garden
author: Liora Fen
authorBio: Liora Fen writes fantasy shaped by craft, apprenticeship, and difficult promises. She lives near a botanical garden and collects broken clocks.
synopsis: Apprentice gardener Nera finds metal roots growing beneath the royal greenhouse in Valenne. When the plants begin copying people's voices, she must identify who planted them before the queen's treaty feast becomes a trap.

title: Good Enough Tomorrow
author: Leah Sorrel
authorBio: Leah Sorrel is a counselor and workshop leader who studies how people sustain small changes. She writes in practical exercises drawn from everyday setbacks.
synopsis: In Bellwick, night-shift nurse Tessa Reed tries to keep healthy habits through a changing schedule. Sorrel uses Tessa's setbacks alongside a new parent's and a returning student's to show how small restarts can keep one missed task from becoming a verdict.

title: The Bridge Keeper
author: Owen Rusk
authorBio: Owen Rusk writes historical fiction centered on workers whose decisions change a community. His novels favor tools, trades, and precise local detail.
synopsis: During the spring flood of 1936, bridge keeper Thomas Bell is ordered to keep a mill road open outside Marlowe. A school bus stalls on the span, leaving Thomas to choose between his employer's orders and the families waiting downstream.

title: Birds Over Briar Lake
author: Ruth Haldane
authorBio: Ruth Haldane is a naturalist whose field writing follows the people who protect ordinary habitats. She has spent many springs counting wetland birds.
synopsis: At Briar Lake, volunteers record the return of marsh birds while a proposed road threatens the reed beds. Haldane follows one breeding season through dawn counts, local hearings, and the patient work of restoring a shoreline.

title: Every Door in June
author: Petra Moss
authorBio: Petra Moss writes romantic comedies about people who make lists and then fall off them. Her work is set in walkable, slightly chaotic cities.
synopsis: Apartment manager Bea Linden has one month to fix a condemned stairwell in Providence, but the building's carpenter is the ex who once left her mid-renovation. Every repair reveals another secret in the walls, and their residents start taking bets on which problem will be solved first.

title: The Quiet Archive
author: Ivo Serrano
authorBio: Ivo Serrano writes suspense about institutions and the people asked to trust them. He previously worked as a records conservator.
synopsis: An archivist in Santa Fe receives a reel labeled with tomorrow's date and the sound of a woman confessing to a fire that has not happened. He identifies her as a museum guard and races to locate the recording's source before someone stages the blaze.

title: The Salt Road Kitchen
author: Fern Bellamy
authorBio: Fern Bellamy writes food memoir rooted in family recipes and working kitchens. She learned to cook beside her aunt at a seaside guesthouse.
synopsis: When Fern inherits her aunt's shuttered guesthouse in Northumberland, she finds a recipe book annotated with the names of former visitors. Reopening the kitchen one supper at a time brings back people whose stories alter what she remembers about her childhood summers.

chapters.title: What Was Left in the Pantry

title: The City Beneath Tuesday
author: Dalia Wren
authorBio: Dalia Wren builds speculative cities around familiar civic problems and improbable solutions. She writes from a small studio above a train station.
synopsis: Every Tuesday, a second city appears below the subway platforms of Holloway, and courier Niko Vale delivers messages between its residents and those above. When the stairs fail to disappear on Wednesday, both cities face a flood from a river neither remembers building.
